rows.subtype: Feeling watched for a group label [Actor]
rows.description: A child told that girls are poor at maths or that children from some schools are weaker feels a knot in the stomach during a test and underperforms. The fear of confirming the label uses up the mental space needed for the problem.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Performing below ability under a label [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager from a group that is assumed to do poorly in a subject grows tense in exams, rushes and doubts known answers. The results look like low ability but come from added pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A student hears a teacher's low expectations, such as surprise at a good grade, and starts believing it. They may disengage to avoid trying and failing under scrutiny.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A teacher or mentor sees a capable student freeze in situations where their group is expected to fail. They notice the pattern of strong practice work and weak high-stakes performance, and do not read it as lack of talent.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A student reminds themselves that a test measures preparation not worth, recalls their past successes and values, and seeks mentors who show belief. Instructors can help by framing tasks as ways to grow and not as verdicts on ability.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child on a shared sports team or class project befriends a classmate from another religion, caste or region and finds the imagined differences small. Personal knowledge chips away at fear learned from others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teacher notices that putting rival groups in the same room, with no shared goal and unequal status, only hardens stereotypes. Contact helps when people work as equals toward a common aim with backing from authority.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Teenagers from different neighbourhoods on a school play or science team depend on each other to succeed. Shared effort turns "them" into "us" more than talks about tolerance do.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Being the only one from your group [Receiver]
rows.description: A young adult who is the sole member of their community in a hostel or workplace feels curious eyes and carries the pressure of representing everyone. Good contact lets them be an individual instead of an example.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young team lead arranges mixed work groups with a real common goal and equal roles, and does not tolerate mockery of any group. They see attitudes soften through shared work, not lectures.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
